CustomField.label: Invitee Title
CustomField.description:
★R8 SEIM_INVITEE.JOB_TITLE. Was a formula reading Event_Attendee__r.Title__c live; it is now a snapshot stamped when the invitee is added, because the reference ERD snapshots it and the business confirmed that is what it wants.
The reason is the one design.md already recorded as a known risk and never fixed: with a live formula, correcting an attendee's title after their invitation was approved silently rewrites what the approval appears to have shown. An approval record that changes after the fact is not a record. The API name is unchanged so every report, report type, layout and approval page that already reads it keeps working — a rename would have been churn for nothing.
What the snapshot costs, and it is the mirror image of what it buys: a typo fixed on the attendee no longer propagates. The invitee keeps the wrong spelling until someone edits that row too.
★R12 That cost is now paid only where it buys something, and Status__c is the line. R8 framed this as a choice between a live formula and a frozen snapshot, and took the frozen one whole. But the audit argument it rests on — "an approval record that changes after the fact is not a record" — only applies once there is an approval to misrepresent. A Draft row has been approved by nobody, so freezing a typo into it protects nothing and simply shows the approver stale data when it is finally submitted.
So the rule is per-status, and EventAttendeeSync enforces it:
- Draft — full re-stamp when the attendee changes. Nothing is frozen yet, including the routing fields, because nothing has been submitted. - Pending — the display snapshots only: Invitee_Salutation__c, Invitee_Title__c, Invitee_Org__c, Cust_Cd__c. An approver should read what is true now. Account__c and Account_Manager__c are deliberately NOT re-stamped: the approver chain was frozen onto Approver_1..5__c at submit, and moving the routing fields underneath a chain already in flight would leave the row describing one approver and addressed to another. - Approved, Rejected — nothing, ever. This is the case R8 was actually arguing about, and R8 wins it unchanged.
Why a trigger rather than reverting to a formula: a formula would sync every status, which is precisely the Approved case R8 ruled out. The automation is not there to reproduce a formula more expensively — it is there because the correct behaviour is conditional and a formula cannot be.
